description: t-SNE on 10,000 synthetic scRNA-seq cells — heavy CPU bubble, targets 70-80% GPU idle
prompt:
Perform t-SNE dimensionality reduction on a synthetic single-cell RNA-seq dataset. Do everything in one code block.

1. Generate a count matrix: 10000 cells × 2000 genes. numpy.random.seed(42). Draw counts from numpy.random.negative_binomial(n=5, p=0.5, size=(10000, 2000)). Multiply each gene column by numpy.random.lognormal(mean=1.0, sigma=1.5, size=2000).
2. Normalize each cell to 10000 total counts, then apply numpy.log1p.
3. Select the top 300 highest-variance genes.
4. Run PCA to 50 components: sklearn.decomposition.PCA(n_components=50, random_state=42).
5. Run t-SNE: sklearn.manifold.TSNE(n_components=2, perplexity=30, n_iter=1000, method='barnes_hut', random_state=42, verbose=1). This will take 3-8 minutes.
6. Run KMeans with 8 clusters on the 2D embedding: sklearn.cluster.KMeans(n_clusters=8, random_state=42, n_init=10).
7. Print cluster sizes sorted by size (cluster_id, n_cells, pct_of_total).

Do not generate any plots. Report only the cluster sizes table.
notes: HEAVY bubble task. sklearn TSNE barnes_hut on 10k × 50 PCA: O(n log n) × 1000 iters, takes 3-8 minutes. GPU is completely idle. Target GPU bubble: 70-80%. This is the 'medium heavy' reference point for t-SNE scaling.
